name: K2c: the winner of J2d/K2a/K2b (J2d) without the log2(operand_tile_traffic_ratio) term (4 weights, current contract, no tm_log_inst)

def score(f, p, hw, w):
    # Raster: the current contract cannot see swizzle, and with no inst_total tie-break every raster variant of a tile
    # scores exactly the same, so which raster runs is outside the rule's control (the harness breaks the tie by config
    # identity). J2d's raster-robust cost: the worst of the two width-1 orientations, max(A-panel, B-panel refetch),
    # scaled by (1 + serial split-K partial bytes / compulsory bytes) (partial round trips evict the panels from L2),
    # times blocks per SM (panel reuse needs K-lockstep; the lockstep window is one CTA per SM).
    ref = np.maximum(f.a_refetch_bw_demand, f.b_refetch_bw_demand) * (1.0 + f.splitk_partial_bytes_ratio)
    d = f.tm_dram_ratio + ref / f.resident_block_scarcity
    # Time model: busiest-SM compute path, L2->SM feed (kappa = w[0]) and DRAM feed incl. raster refetch, p=2 norm.
    t = np.sqrt(np.square(f.tm_crit_ratio) + np.square(w[0] * f.tm_l2_ratio) + np.square(d))
    s = 10.0 * np.log2(t)
    # Efficiency the norm cannot see: register-staged 2-stage mainloop, CTA-wide barrier over more warps.
    s = s + w[1] * f.tm_regstaged + w[2] * f.tm_cta_warps
    # Split-K time model with an interior optimum, in log2 time.
    s = s + w[3] * f.splitk_roofline_log_time
    return s
